subject: MSA & Order Form — Term Fade / Auto‑Renew Decision Runbook
content:
From: Dana Park <dana.park@anchorgrid.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Jamie Ellis <jamie.ellis@anchorgrid.com>, AnchorGrid Legal <legal@anchorgrid.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form — term mechanics questions

Marcus,

Thanks for the updated MSA redline (v3). Our CFO and procurement team pushed back on a couple of term-related items and asked us to confirm AnchorGrid's expectations before we escalate to legal. Quick summary:

- Auto‑renew length: the order form shows 12‑month auto‑renewal unless notice is provided 60 days prior. Procurement is requesting 30 days.
- Term fade / ramp-down: AnchorGrid wants a 90‑day transition assistance period for data export and handback; our procurement wants to cap that at 30 days.
- Termination for convenience (TFC): they expect a 60‑day notice with pro‑rated refund; our finance prefers no refunds for TFC if usage exceeded minimums.

Could you confirm Redwood's flexibility on notice windows and the standard runbook for a phase‑out (data + jobs + keys)? We can loop in legal next if there's wiggle room.

Attachments: AG_MSA_redline_v3.docx (redline), OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf

Thanks,
Dana
Head of Procurement
AnchorGrid Inc.

-----

On Wed, Jun 9, 2026 at 10:08 AM, marcus_lin@redwood.com wrote:
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Dana Park <dana.park@anchorgrid.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — term mechanics questions

Dana —

Appreciate the clear summary. High level answers below; details and the operational checklist are attached (mutual-action-plan.xlsx).

- Auto‑renew notice window: Standard Redwood practice is 60 days for annual commitments, but we can accept 30 days for pilots or teams under $250k TCV. For AnchorGrid, given expected TCV, we can offer a 45‑day compromise.
- Transition assistance (runout): We normally provide 90 days for enterprise migrations with dedicated handback support; we can offer 45 days with limited handback for commercial pilots. We recommend the 90‑day model when there are data egress/transfer complexities.
- TFC refunds: We are willing to offer pro‑rated refunds for unused pre‑paid amounts if termination is initiated before commit midpoint; otherwise standard practice is no refund if minimums were met.

Action items I propose:
1) Karthik to confirm legal comfort on mixing a 45‑day notice/45‑day runout compromise.
2) Olivia (Olga) to draft a short amendment to the Order Form documenting runout obligations and SLA during handback.
3) Marcus to propose the mutual action plan with timelines attached.

Can you confirm AnchorGrid's preference (30 / 45 / 60) on the notice and whether you need full 90 days for data export?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx

-----

On Thu, Jun 10, 2026 at 09:42 AM, karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Dana Park <dana.park@anchorgrid.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — term mechanics questions

Dana / Marcus —

Quick legal perspective: we are comfortable with a 45‑day notice concession and a 45‑day runout for the AnchorGrid pilot, provided the Order Form ties the runout to a defined handback checklist (data export format, runbook for job cancellation, KV cache purge and key rotation timeline). We need the Order Form to state:

- Notice window (45 days) and effective termination date definition
- Runout obligations (45 days) with Redwood responsibilities vs. customer responsibilities (who runs exports, who covers egress costs)
- TFC refund trigger: pro rata only if termination occurs before 50% of the prepaid term; no refund thereafter

Karthik
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

-----

On Fri, Jun 11, 2026 at 16:25:00 -07:00, Dana Park <dana.park@anchorgrid.com> wrote:
From: Dana Park <dana.park@anchorgrid.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Jamie Ellis <jamie.ellis@anchorgrid.com>, AnchorGrid Legal <legal@anchorgrid.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2026 16:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — term mechanics questions

Thanks — the 45/45 compromise sounds workable. A few clarifications from our side before we send this to our legal: 

- Can Redwood confirm whether egress bandwidth and storage during the 45‑day runout are billed at standard rates or waived for one export?
- We would like the runout checklist to include a defined handback acceptance criteria (hash check / sample data validation).
- For the TFC refund trigger: can we move the cutoff to 40% of the prepaid term instead of 50%? Our finance prefers an earlier refund threshold for pilot economics.

If Redwood can accept egress waived for one full export and a 40% refund trigger, we can route to legal and sign an amendment quickly.

Dana
Head of Procurement
AnchorGrid Inc.

Attachments referenced: AG_MSA_redline_v3.docx, OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf
